items.title: Live: Ben Carroll sworn in as Victorian premier, immediately calls construction royal commission
items.description: Ben Carroll has been appointed premier of Victoria. Follow our live coverage.

items.title: Reserve Bank governor warns world facing increased supply shocks
items.description: The Reserve Bank governor says the world has become more shock-prone in recent years, and the latest oil spike is a complication for the central bank's monetary policy.

items.title: 'Shake down Angus for 10k': NSW Libs faction's texts in ICAC spotlight
items.description: The NSW corruption watchdog has heard claims senior Liberal figures discussed seeking financial backing for the party's right-wing faction from now-federal Opposition Leader Angus Taylor.

items.title: AI just had its Sarah Connor moment. Is Australia ready?
items.description: Far-fetched scenarios about artificial intelligence became more realistic last week when an OpenAI model hacked another company.

items.title: Australians may have unknowingly eaten horse meat, secret documents show
items.description: Government documents show hundreds of businesses operating in Australia have breached food safety laws, with one politician warning "you could be eating a minced horse".

items.title: Origin Energy believes 900,000 customers' data accessed in breach
items.description: Origin Energy says it started reviewing a "potential security threat" early this month but deemed it not credible, before new information indicated a breach.

items.title: KPMG to be grilled at parliamentary inquiry on secretly stashing client files
items.description: Accounting firm KPMG will be hauled before a federal inquiry to answer further questions about why one of its former employees stored printed copies of confidential Lendlease board documents in her locker and shared them with her colleagues to win audit contracts.

items.title: Harvey Norman and Latitude face $55m penalty for misleading ad campaign
items.description: The two businesses misled customers into taking out credit cards and paying additional fees in a 60-month interest-free payment scheme, the corporate regulator says.

items.title: Australian-founded restaurant at centre of South Korean court case over ant garnish
items.description: Seoul prosecutors have alleged Evett in Seoul's Gangnam district served ants illegally imported from Thailand and the US in violation of food safety regulations.

items.title: Rabbi supports stopping hospital staff from wearing Israeli, Palestinian pins
items.description: Jewish patients requested their religion be removed from their hospital admission information following allegations nurses made menacing comments about Israeli patients, the royal commission on antisemitism has heard.

items.title: Embattled MP Moira Deeming resigns from Victorian Liberal Party
items.description: Moira Deeming says she will remain in parliament as an independent, after having her candidacy revoked by the Liberal party earlier this month.

items.title: Hobart councillor rebukes 'manufactured crisis' over snack saga
items.description: Councillors at the City of Hobart say they are unable to share the outcome of a motion heard behind closed doors at last night's meeting, which called for an investigation into the conduct of the deputy lord mayor.

items.title: Search for missing two-month-old boy continues off SA coast
items.description: The bodies of the boy's mother and sister were found floating in the ocean yesterday, after authorities were called to Cape Northumberland, about 400 kilometres south-east of Adelaide.

items.title: US and Iran in 'good talks' Trump says as support for war wanes
items.description: US President Donald Trump says the United States is having "good talks" with Iran, and there is a chance of a deal over their conflict, but he warns that US strikes will resume if the negotiations fail to deliver.

items.title: Why I was a chronic people pleaser — and what worked instead
items.description: For me, people pleasing was a coping mechanism that developed over time out of vigilance, responsibility and love for my family. But there was a better way.

items.title: 'Straight to the pool room': Film classic The Castle goes on stage
items.description: The feature film responsible for Australian sayings such as ''Tell him he's dreaming'' is being launched as a stage production.

items.title: Struggling to save? Here are five ways to curb your impulse spending
items.description: If you'd rather be saving than shopping, but are struggling to switch gears, there are ways to change your habits.

items.title: Salmon farming transformed Norway. Now it's facing the consequences
items.description: Norway's salmon industry is a global behemoth 18 times the size of Tasmania's. But the country's success holds a warning for Australia.

items.title: Matthew Cox to stand trial for alleged Rockhampton killings of wife and baby
items.description: A man accused of murdering his wife Tayla Black, 30, and 11-week-old baby daughter Murphy at a central Queensland home will face a criminal trial.

items.title: Melbourne businessman found guilty of rape
items.description: A County Court jury has found beyond reasonable doubt that the man, who can't be named for legal reasons, raped and sexually assaulted a woman at his home in March 2023.

items.title: Tate brothers to remain in jail at least two more weeks
items.description: A federal US judge says social media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate will remain in jail for at least two more weeks until their next hearing as they fight extradition.

items.title: Twin tragedies leave community, nursing colleagues in shock
items.description: The car crash death of mother-of-two Elaine Gee and the stabbing of another woman will send "ripples" through the Tasmanian community, a family violence support service says.

items.title: The sun has set on the British Empire, and yet this celebration remains
items.description: The Commonwealth Games continues to roll on despite calls to decolonise our lives, with Scotland of all places a strange venue to stage two celebrations of the British Empire over the past 12 years.

items.title: AFL clubs explore facial recognition as new ticketing method
items.description: Facial recognition technology is being used as an alternative form of ticketing, but some experts are concerned it could open the door to the data being used for more than just event entry.

items.title: Australia should brace for war impact to get worse, Treasury warns
items.description: The federal government is yet to reveal whether it will extend the fuel excise discount, which is set to expire this week.
